It builds Float cumulative symbol costs, compares run costs by cumulative endpoint subtraction, and tests savings using a Double threshold; the threshold 21/22 fixtures and the large cumulative-rounding witness exercise these details. kLZ77 ports the 2^20-window hash chain (chain length 256, zero-run chain), the one-step lazy match and the static LenCost/DistCost tables (Double literals rounded to Float); kOptimal reprices with a SymbolCostEstimator over the greedy result (flat rows, so absent symbols cost 0 or 12 as in the source) and keeps its shortest path without a second threshold. No image widths reach these callers, so there are no special distances. Forced prefix codes write min_symbol 512 by the U32 selectors, and kBest clustering prices histograms past 256 symbols at FLT_MAX as ANSPopulationCost does. LZ77Tests check hand traces of the cited source (tripled run, lazy match, greedy and optimal), the gain threshold for kRLE/kLZ77/kOptimal and expansion of all three on a 6,000-token mixed stream. The jpeg-witness decodes kOptimal and kLZ77 coded ICCs (desc4, desc1000, random40000) and reports their LZ77 flag; the parse itself is pinned by Swift tests, since no harness command compares token streams. Floating-point contraction is unverified: clang on arm64 may fuse `total_cost += cost * counts[j]` (AddSymbolCost) into an FMA, while Swift rounds the product separately. Like libjxl, kOptimal is quadratic in the worst case, because the run skip bounds only repeat-previous runs.
